items.prompt: Select every correct statement about the simplified retina.

options.text: Light passes through the ganglion-cell layer before reaching rods and cones.
Neural information passes from photoreceptors through bipolar pathways toward ganglion cells.
The optic nerve carries incoming light to the rods.
The optic disc has the highest density of cones.

items.cue: Separate the light route, information route and nerve exit.
items.explanation: Light reaches photoreceptors after passing through the overlying retinal layers. Information then passes toward ganglion cells, whose axons carry neural signals in the optic nerve.

items.prompt: Select every correct contribution to balance.

options.text: Semicircular canals detect changes in head rotation.
Proprioceptors provide information about limb position.
Visual information can help the brain maintain balance.
The cochlea is the main detector of straight-line acceleration.

items.cue: Balance combines vestibular, visual and body-position information.
items.explanation: Canals contribute rotational information, proprioceptors contribute body-position information and vision adds another source. The cochlea is used for hearing.

items.prompt: Select every correct statement about pituitary routes.

options.text: ADH is made in hypothalamic neurons.
ADH is released into blood from the posterior pituitary.
Anterior-pituitary cells make and release their own hormones.
All pituitary hormones are made in the posterior pituitary.

items.explanation: The anterior pituitary produces its own hormones. ADH is produced in the hypothalamus and transported to the posterior pituitary for storage and release.

items.prompt: Select every correct comparison of ADH and aldosterone.

options.text: ADH directly increases collecting-duct water permeability.
Both hormones have identical immediate kidney actions.
Aldosterone is released by the adrenal cortex.

items.cue: Compare the immediate kidney action and release site.
items.explanation: ADH changes water permeability. Aldosterone from the adrenal cortex changes sodium and potassium handling. Their effects on body fluid overlap, but their immediate actions differ.
